candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort → Nutrition and Oral Hydration: monitor hydration status, provide oral fluids as appropriate, and implement individualized dietary/fluid modifications based on diagnosis and client needs.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — individualized oral fluid management in heart failure
candidate.educational_objective: When a heart-failure client has a prescribed fluid limit, teach accurate daily tracking and adherence to the individualized plan without applying a universal restriction to all heart-failure clients.

options.A: Track total fluid intake across the day and follow the individualized amount recommended by the health care team rather than applying a standard limit used for all clients with heart failure.
options.B: Stop all oral fluids because complete fluid avoidance is the safest approach whenever heart failure is present.
options.C: Use the same fixed fluid limit for every client with heart failure regardless of symptoms, sodium level, or clinical status.
options.D: Ignore the prescribed limit because fluid intake does not contribute to volume management in heart failure.

candidate.rationale: Current American Heart Association self-care guidance states that people with heart failure may be advised to limit fluid intake and should ask their health care professional how much fluid to drink each day; it also recommends tracking daily fluid intake. The AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline notes that evidence for routine fluid restriction is limited, so restriction should not be converted into a universal fixed rule for every person with heart failure. Therefore, A is correct. B is unsafe overrestriction, C ignores individualized clinical assessment, and D contradicts the role of fluid management in selected clients.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports daily fluid tracking when advised, following a health-care-team-directed amount, and avoiding a universal fluid-restriction rule for all heart-failure clients.
candidate.source_document_title: Lifestyle Changes for Heart Failure; 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
candidate.source_locator: AHA Lifestyle Changes for Heart Failure → 'Track your daily fluid intake': the health care team might recommend limiting liquid intake; talk with the health care professional about how much liquid to drink every day. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline → Section 8.2, Nonpharmacological Management: Advanced HF: fluid restriction is commonly prescribed but evidence is low quality and clinical-outcome benefit is limited/uncertain, supporting individualized rather than universal restriction.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association; American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
candidate.source_version_date: AHA patient guidance current 2026; HF guideline 2022-04-01
candidate.stem: A client with heart failure has been given an individualized daily fluid limit by the health care team. Which teaching by the nurse is most appropriate?
